The second uses the unsigned-incidence alternating component kernel, including isolates and a balanced-component all-ones criterion; the third uses R^T injectivity and complement constraints. Positive sink rates yield strict decay on the bright subspace, so absorption from maximally mixed initial state equals R(F)/binom(n,2). For n≥7 quadrilateral and triangle-plus-pendant each use four sites but give ranks 8 and 9.
